edges.description: RGC-specific Syncrip knockout reproduces the superficial cortical layer defect and causes learning and memory impairment.
edges.limitations: The model is a complete conditional knockout, whereas human SYNCRIP-NDD results from heterozygous haploinsufficiency; mouse cortical neurogenesis also lacks human-specific outer radial glia / OSVZ biology.

edges.description: The knockout mice show learning and memory impairment, a behavioral correlate of the human cognitive phenotype.
edges.limitations: Mouse learning/memory assays are an imperfect proxy for human intellectual disability, and the model is a complete knockout rather than the human heterozygous state.

nodes.description: Reduced hnRNP-Q disturbs the intracellular localization of its target mRNAs in neurons -- hnRNP-Q normally positions mRNAs (including Cdc42-pathway transcripts) in neurites -- altering where those transcripts and their encoded proteins are available during neuronal morphogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: hnRNP Q regulates Cdc42-mediated neuronal morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: The RNA-binding protein hnRNP Q has been implicated in neuronal mRNA metabolism.

nodes.description: Disturbed neuronal mRNA regulation during brain development yields abnormal cortical and synaptic maturation, manifesting as the developmental, cognitive, and neurobehavioral phenotype.
The radial glial temporal transcription program stalls, disrupting late-stage neurogenesis and the ordered deep-to-superficial generation of cortical neurons.

nodes.description: The mutant SYNCRIP protein undergoes weakened liquid-liquid phase separation and fails to form the stabilization complexes (biomolecular condensates) through which SYNCRIP normally maintains temporal transcription-factor programs. This is a property of the mutant protein, shown for pathogenic human variants.
